title: Eucharistic Examination of Conscience
description: An examination specifically focused on preparing to receive the Eucharist worthily and growing in appreciation of this Most Blessed Sacrament.
source: Based on Catholic Teaching on the Eucharist

categories.title: Faith in the Real Presence
categories.description: Reflecting on our belief in Christ's true presence in the Eucharist.

items.text: Have I doubted or denied that Jesus is truly present—Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity—in the Eucharist?
items.clarification: The Church teaches that in the Eucharist, Christ is present in a unique way that transforms the bread and wine into His Body and Blood.

items.text: Have I failed to acknowledge the Eucharist as the 'source and summit' of Christian life?
Have I approached Communion routinely, without awareness of the sacred gift I am receiving?
Have I taken time to ponder the mystery of the Eucharist and grow in my understanding of this sacrament?
Have I neglected to show proper reverence to the Blessed Sacrament through genuflection, silence, or adoration?
Have I spoken about the Eucharist with reverence and defended this teaching when challenged?

categories.title: Preparation for Receiving Communion
categories.description: Considering how we prepare ourselves to receive the Eucharist worthily.

items.text: Have I received Communion while conscious of unconfessed mortal sin?
items.clarification: The Church teaches that we must be in a state of grace to receive Communion worthily (1 Cor 11:27-29).

items.text: Have I observed the one-hour fast before receiving Communion (unless exempted for medical reasons)?
Have I attended Mass hastily or distractedly, without preparing my heart to encounter Christ?
Have I arrived late to Mass without good reason or left early before the final blessing?
Have I dressed modestly and appropriately for Mass, recognizing I am entering God's house?
Have I taken time for prayer before Mass to prepare my heart and mind?
Have I approached the altar with reverence and received the Eucharist with attention and devotion?
Have I allowed myself to be distracted during Mass by my phone, idle thoughts, or conversations?

categories.title: Thanksgiving After Communion
categories.description: Reflecting on how we express gratitude for the gift of the Eucharist.

items.text: Have I taken time for prayer and thanksgiving after receiving Communion?
items.clarification: The moments after receiving Communion are precious for intimate prayer with Christ truly present within us.

items.text: Have I left Mass immediately after Communion without grave reason?
Have I expressed gratitude to God for the gift of the Eucharist?
Have I rushed through or neglected post-Communion reflection?
Have I asked Jesus to transform me through His presence within me?

categories.title: Communion with the Church
categories.description: Examining our unity with the Church that flows from the Eucharist.

items.text: Have I maintained communion with the Church by accepting all her teachings?
items.clarification: The Eucharist both signifies and brings about the unity of the Church. Receiving Communion implies being in communion with the Church's faith.

items.text: Have I deliberately rejected Church teachings while still presenting myself for Communion?
Have I prayed for the unity of all Christians, which the Eucharist signifies and promotes?
Have I fostered division in my parish community through gossip, criticism, or factionalism?
Have I prayed for the Pope, my bishop, and clergy in their ministry of uniting the Church?
Have I made efforts to heal divisions and promote reconciliation in my family and community?

categories.title: Honoring the Lord's Day
categories.description: Reflecting on how we observe Sunday as a day centered on the Eucharist.

items.text: Have I missed Mass on Sundays or Holy Days of Obligation without serious reason?
items.clarification: The Sunday Eucharist is the foundation and confirmation of all Christian practice, which is why the Church teaches it is a grave obligation.

items.text: Have I treated Sunday as a day for the Lord, centered on the Eucharist and rest?
Have I unnecessarily engaged in work or activities that hinder proper observance of Sunday?
Have I helped others, especially family members, to participate in Sunday Mass?
Have I made Sunday a day of family togetherness, joy, and renewal?
Have I extended Sunday worship into works of mercy and service to others?

categories.title: Living a Eucharistic Life
categories.description: Considering how we extend the grace of the Eucharist into our daily lives.

items.text: Have I allowed the Eucharist to transform my life, becoming more giving and self-sacrificial?
items.clarification: The Eucharist is not just a sacred moment during Mass, but should transform our entire lives to be more Christ-like.

items.text: Have I lived Monday through Saturday in a way that contradicts what I profess and receive on Sunday?
Have I shared with others, especially the poor and needy, reflecting Christ's gift of Himself?
Have I recognized Christ in the poor, the suffering, and the marginalized?
Have I worked to build a more just society, inspired by the communion I share in the Eucharist?
Have I allowed the peace of Christ received in Communion to shape how I treat others?
Have I been a witness to others of the joy and transformation that comes from the Eucharist?

categories.title: Eucharistic Adoration and Devotion
categories.description: Reflecting on our devotion to Christ in the Blessed Sacrament outside of Mass.

items.text: Have I made time to visit Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament for adoration when possible?
items.clarification: Eucharistic adoration extends and intensifies the communion with Christ begun at Mass.

items.text: Have I encouraged others to discover the gift of Eucharistic adoration?
Have I participated in Eucharistic processions or devotions when available?
Have I made spiritual communions when unable to receive sacramentally?
Have I taken time to simply be in Christ's presence, allowing Him to transform me through adoration?
Have I developed a personal relationship with Jesus through prayer before the Blessed Sacrament?
